_comment: Public page routes deliberately NOT linked from the landing page, each with
the reason. A ratchet in both directions: a new entry means somebody shipped
a page nobody can reach, and an entry that stops being true must be deleted
in the same commit that links it — the known_failures.txt rule, for the same
/gas was the first thing this caught: a real public page — live gas across
seven chains, whose own meta description promises 'unreadable chains omitted,
never invented' — linked from nowhere. It is in the footer now rather than in
this file, which is the outcome this list exists to force.

routes./reset: Password-reset entry. Reached only by the emailed link, and it carries a token — advertising it on the landing page invites people to load it without one, which can only render an error.
routes./verify: Email-verification entry, same shape as /reset: the link IS the credential.
routes./wallet-link: Entered from the wallet-connect flow with state already established. Landing straight on it out of context has nothing to act on.
routes./signal: One signal's thesis, opened from a stream row as /signal?key=. A bare landing link has no id, so the page can only say the link has none.
routes./admin: The operator's settings page. It is linked from the dashboard for the operator only; every other account would land on a refusal, so the public landing page does not advertise it.
routes./study: The address people guess for the Study Room, whose door is labelled that; it answers a navigation page to /learn and is not a page of its own, so the landing page links /learn.
routes./botcheck: The custodial-bot check is served only when BOTCHECK_ENABLED is 1, true, yes, or on. Otherwise the page answers 404, so the landing page must not link a door that is closed.
routes./rwa: behind the RWA flag, off. It answers 404.
routes./hrc: Operator preview of the Hyperliquid borrow-rate cap. The public gets 404, including while HRC_ENABLED is on, so the landing page does not advertise it.
routes./tools: Operator catalog of runtime tools. It is not a public page, the card says coming soon, and the landing page does not link it.
